text: What does a mutual fund company earn on every hundred rupees it looks after?
At ICICI Prudential, fifty three paise a year, by its own measure. It keeps thirty seven as profit, before tax.
In April, the rule on what a fund may charge was trimmed.
The company says that had no negative impact on it.
In July, an analyst asked: was it fair to assume that you have passed on all to the distributors? The finance chief answered in one word. Yes.
Distributors are the sellers: agents and banks. But this is the fund house's own account. No document we read shows what any seller was paid.
So who gave way? As we read it, the sellers. And it all starts with one question:
